summary: Cold-start handshake mismatch in multi-region prewarm causes intermittent cross-variant fallbacks
description:
Issue summary:
During a staged canary for customer Formly Analytics (dedicated pool), a subset of tenant traffic experienced unexpected fallback to a legacy variant during cold-start spikes. The routing divergence coincided with cross-region prewarm activities and produced mixed-model outputs for affected sessions.

Impact:
- ~2–5% of Formly production requests between 2026-03-10T04:10 and 2026-03-10T04:45 UTC were routed to an older model variant, causing correctness regressions and billing spikes for the customer.
- Customer reported degraded classification accuracy in their pipeline and opened a support call (this ticket).

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant pool (Formly Analytics) on reserved capacity across us-west-2 primary with us-east-1 prewarm mirror.
- Model config: open-lama-7b-v2 (primary), rw-internal-compat-7b (legacy fallback).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Initiate a canary weight change (10% -> 30%) with prewarm mirror enabled across regions.
2) Autoscaler launches a new serving shard in us-east-1 and begins prewarm handshake (KV-cache warm & session migrate).
3) Edge proxies forward initial cold-start requests; orchestrator attempts to reconcile pin state with the new shard while the prewarm handshake is still pending.
4) A subset of sessions lose pin affinity and are routed to the legacy variant for the next 1–3 requests before affinity is reestablished.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Orchestrator trace: multiple "pin_consensus_timeout" entries for tenant Formly-8934 around 2026-03-10T04:12Z.
- Edge proxy logs: repeated 200 responses but with model_id header switching between open-lama-7b-v2 and rw-internal-compat-7b within same session.
- Serving runtime: increased cold-start latency on the new shards (KV cache miss ratio ~0.84).
- Metrics: small spike in fallback rate (fallbacks_to_legacy_variant) concurrent with prewarm-handshake-duration metric > 12s.

Customer note:
Formly SRE flagged higher-than-normal billing and an accuracy regression for their classification endpoint. They requested an immediate mitigation to stop cross-region prewarm behavior for their tenant.

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Disable cross-region prewarm mirroring for the Formly tenant until root cause is fixed.

Additional context:
This reproduces reliably when prewarm handshakes overlap with a canary weight increase and when the edge pool is under a brief connection churn (we observed several short TCP reconnects during the window). The pattern is not a full orchestrator crash but a timing coordination issue between pin commit and prewarm completion.
comments: 2026-03-10T05:01Z - Maya Singh (Support): Initial triage complete, escalated to SRE. Noted pin_consensus_timeout entries. Contacted customer to confirm impact window.

2026-03-10T05:22Z - SRE Team (Diego Ramos): Reproduced in staging by simulating shard prewarm + canary roll; observed session stickiness flips for ~1–3 requests. Captured orchestrator trace IDs: trace-usr-A12B, trace-usr-A12C.
2026-03-10T06:10Z - Formly (Customer): Confirmed they see mixed outputs in analytics. Asked for immediate disable of mirroring; granted by ops.

2026-03-11T09:45Z - Diego Ramos: Applied customer-scoped mitigation to disable cross-region prewarm mirroring for tenant Formly-8934. Fall back rate dropped to baseline. Preparing PR to harden handshake.
2026-03-12T14:30Z - Product (Lina Park): Requested postmortem and proposed changes to prewarm handshake timeouts and pin commit ordering.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Pin commit occurs only after prewarm completes; if prewarm handshake extends beyond a pin_consensus_timeout, orchestrator allows fallback routing path while awaiting commit.
Hypothesis 2: Edge-proxy connection churn caused duplicate session tokens to be evaluated on different orchestrator leaders, exposing a consensus edge case.
Reproduction: Automated test in staging reproduced with 95/100 runs when injected 10–30% TCP reconnect probability during shard prewarm; fallback observed in 2–6% of sessions.
Trace analysis: Orchestrator traces show pin_commit event delayed by 8–15s in problematic runs due to blocking KV cache warm jobs on the new shard thread pool.
resolution: Immediate mitigation: disabled cross-region prewarm mirroring for the Formly tenant and pinned their traffic to the stable variant until fix lands. Longer-term fix: change prewarm handshake to publish a provisional pin and make pin_consensus_timeout adaptive; also throttle KV cache warm jobs to prevent blocking main commit path. PRs opened to implement handshake adjustment and to add a canary safety check before weight increases.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11: Ops disabled mirroring for Formly-8934 (rollback command: ops disable-mirror --tenant Formly-8934).
PR #5823 (routing): add provisional pin publish and canary-safety check under feature flag.
PR #5871 (orchestrator): make pin_consensus_timeout adaptive based on prewarm duration metrics and avoid blocking on KV warm tasks for commit path.
Follow-up: add e2e test that exercises prewarm+canary timing and a new observability metric fallback_rate_by_handshake_phase. Owner: Diego Ramos. ETA: 2026-03-25.
Customer communication: Sent mitigation summary and planned fixes; scheduled a sync on 2026-03-13 to review rollout plan with Formly.
Postmortem required: Yes — link to be added once authored.
